title: I Let the Roommate Keep the Temperature Schedule He Programmed

parts.text: I woke at 5:50 a.m. to a 62-degree living room because Mateo had programmed eco nights in the thermostat app he insisted we share. The lease addendum, which he printed, said 68 minimum when anyone is home. I was twenty-eight, WFH, in a hoodie. He was asleep. I screenshotted the schedule, the addendum, and the indoor sensor. Then I set the app to follow the addendum exactly, including his 2 a.m. gaming hours when he liked it at 72. At 6:04 the app notified him of a schedule change he had granted me admin to make.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He granted me admin; the addendum is now the schedule including his 2 a.m. 72.

social.video_title: Eco nights versus a printed 68 minimum — Part 1/2
social.description: WFH hoodie, 62 degrees, he was asleep. Admin was on. Would you have waited until a meeting?

parts.text: Mateo uninstalled the app, which did not uninstall physics. 68 held. His 2 a.m. 72 lasted one night until he asked to renegotiate like adults. We did: 68 nights, 70 days, no stealth eco. I kept admin. Hoodies became optional. The addendum stayed on the fridge. Shared apps are constitutions. He programmed it. I believed the paper. The sensor stopped arguing.

social.description: Renegotiated numbers, fridge addendum, optional hoodie. Was eco a lease?
